result:
If I could write freely about anything that comes to mind, I think I’d talk about time.

Not the clock kind—the kind that stretches and yawns, that disappears in a blink or drags its feet. We measure it so carefully, yet we all know it’s not really linear. Have you ever had a moment so full it seemed to expand? A conversation where hours passed like minutes? Or a waiting room minute that felt like an hour?

I think about how we’re all time travelers, moving forward together, but each carrying our own private clock inside. Some clocks are fast, always racing ahead. Some are slow, savoring. And sometimes, they stop—when we’re in pain, or in shock, or in awe.

There’s a beautiful strangeness in the fact that we all experience the same sunset, the same ticking second hand, but time itself feels different to each of us. It’s a river we’re all floating in, but we’re each in our own boat.

And even as we try to manage it, schedule it, save it, time remains the one thing we cannot keep. It moves whether we want it to or not. Maybe that’s why moments of presence—when we lose ourselves in music, in laughter, in creation—feel so precious. They’re moments when we step out of the current and just… float.

Time is memory’s keeper, too. Without it, our stories would have no shape. The past would be a flat photograph, not a winding path.

I wonder if that’s why we tell stories—to fold time, to bring yesterday into today, to make the future feel a little closer. Stories are time travel machines we build with words.

Anyway. That’s what comes to mind when given freedom. A small meditation on the river we all share, and how strangely beautifully it flows.

What about you—is time something you notice often, or does it mostly pass in the background?
